To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
molecular simulations and 3-D-RISM calculations can provide accurate quantitative estimates of ion distributions in nucleic acid solutions, but that NLPB calculations are less reliable.
the number of ions condensed around DNA is well reproduced by MD simulation and 2D-RISM theory, but not by NLPB theory, and that the ionic atmosphere extends to ∼25 Å.
MD simulation and three-dimensional reference interaction-site model calculations provide quantitative insight into ion distributions in solution and the ion atmosphere around DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of molecular simulation techniques to the characterization of the ionic atmospheres around DNA and RNA.
understanding how ions interact with and influence DNA.
the development of a theoretical framework for understanding the structure and stability of nucleic acids in aqueous solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
3D-Rism and MD simulation provide the best estimates of condensed ions around DNA and NLPB is the worst, and the difference is significant.
3D-RIMS is the most reliable method, but the results are still in need of further refinement.
the ionic atmosphere near DNA remains only partially understood and that MD simulations, 3D-Rism and NLPB calculations are not in full agreement with the experimental IC data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MD simulations and 3DRISM calculations provide a good description of the ion distributions around DNA at physiological salt concentrations, but at high ionic strength the ionic atmosphere is not fully captured by either of these methods.
3D-Rism and MD simulations are able to capture the ionic atmosphere of nucleic acids, while NLPB calculations do not.
MD simulations and 3DRISM are both able to provide a reasonable description for ion distribution around nucleic acid molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion atmosphere around duplex DNA remains incompletely understood at the atomic-level detail.
the ion atmosphere around DNA is complex and depends strongly on the DNA sequence and the salt concentration.
the number of condensed ions around DNA is sensitive to the concentration of NaCl(aq).
